Let

```math
m_k=\mathbb E(\Theta^k).
```

Because conditional on `\Theta=\theta`, the `X_i`'s are i.i.d. Bernoulli`(\theta)`,

```math
\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_k=1)=\mathbb E(\Theta^k)=m_k .
```

Hence the assumptions give

```math
m_0=1,\qquad m_1=\frac12,\qquad m_2=\frac13,\qquad m_3=\frac14,\qquad m_4=r.
```

After four successes,

```math
p_\mu=\mathbb P(X_5=1\mid X_1=\cdots=X_4=1) =\frac{\mathbb E(\Theta^5)}{\mathbb E(\Theta^4)} =\frac{m_5}{r}.
```

So the problem is to determine the possible range of `m_5` given the first five moments.

---

### 1. Moment constraints for `m_5`

Let

```math
s=m_5.
```

For a probability measure on `[0,1]`, the truncated Hausdorff moment conditions say that the matrices

```math
H_1=(m_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^{2}
```

and

```math
H_0-H_1=(m_{i+j}-m_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^{2}
```

must both be positive semidefinite.

The first matrix is

```math
H_1= \begin{pmatrix} \frac12&\frac13&\frac14\\ \frac13&\frac14&r\\ \frac14&r&s \end{pmatrix}.
```

Its determinant is

```math
\det(H_1) =-\frac{288r^2-96r-8s+9}{576}.
```

Positive semidefiniteness gives

```math
288r^2-96r-8s+9\le0,
```

therefore

```math
s\ge 36r^2-12r+\frac98 .
```

---

The second matrix is

```math
H_0-H_1= \begin{pmatrix} \frac12&\frac16&\frac1{12}\\ \frac16&\frac1{12}&\frac14-r\\ \frac1{12}&\frac14-r&r-s \end{pmatrix}.
```

Its determinant is

```math
\det(H_0-H_1) =-\frac{864r^2-408r+24s+43}{1728}.
```

Hence

```math
864r^2-408r+24s+43\le0,
```

so

```math
s\le -36r^2+17r-\frac{43}{24}.
```

The remaining principal-minor conditions are automatically satisfied whenever the given four moments are feasible. Thus the complete range of the fifth moment is

```math
36r^2-12r+\frac98 \le m_5\le -36r^2+17r-\frac{43}{24}.
```

---

### 2. Convert to `p_\mu`

Since

```math
p_\mu=\frac{m_5}{r},
```

and `r>0` (indeed `m_4\ge m_3^2/m_2=3/16`), divide the whole interval by `r`:

```math
\boxed{ \frac{36r^2-12r+\frac98}{r} \le p_\mu\le \frac{-36r^2+17r-\frac{43}{24}}{r} }
```

or equivalently,

```math
\boxed{ 36r-12+\frac{9}{8r} \le p_\mu\le -36r+17-\frac{43}{24r} }.
```

Therefore, for every feasible value of `r`, the set of all possible posterior probabilities is exactly

```math
\boxed{ p_\mu\in \left[ 36r-12+\frac{9}{8r}, \; -36r+17-\frac{43}{24r} \right]. }
```

The endpoints are attainable because the extremal truncated Hausdorff moment problems are realized by discrete measures on `[0,1]` (principal representations), so this is the full possible range rather than only necessary bounds.
